info.name: AudioEqualiser
info.comment: A parametric equaliser for an Audio mixing chain.

description.p: Create as a child of an Audio object or set the inherited Audio field. Use Channel to process one channel set, or leave it at zero to process the global mix. Bands run in list order.

The Bands and Gain form one configuration that is applied to every channel of the processing layout, with independent filter history for each channel. The equaliser does not perform bass management and is not an automatic crossover for an LFE channel. Application equalisers accept live changes; global equalisers become immutable after initialisation.

The top-level parameters are available as the fields Gain, Loudness and ListeningLevel. Each band is an AudioEQBand with a type, frequency, gain and Q, and up to 64 bands are permitted. Band gain is ignored by pass filters, and Q is limited to one for shelf filters, where it sets the shelf slope. Use InsertBand, SetBand and RemoveBand to edit individual bands, GetBand to read one, and Bands to read or replace the whole list.

Field writes and band methods before initialisation are range-checked and stored, and Init() validates the complete configuration. After initialisation each call is validated and applied immediately, as a single change.
The following adds a bass shelf to a playing channel set and lowers the output trim:
description.pre: eq = obj.new('AudioEqualiser', { audio=audio, channel=channel }) check eq.mtInsertBand(0, struct.new('AudioEQBand', { type=EQB_LOW_SHELF, frequency=100, gain=4, q=0.7 })) eq.gain = -2
description.p: The same parameters are published through the inherited AudioEffect schema. The top-level keys are gain, loudness and listening_level, and the bands group has type, frequency, gain and q members. Use AudioEffect.Batch() to change several of them in a single step, e.g. a band and the output trim together:
A band inserted by AudioEffect.Batch() is a silent peak filter at 1000 Hz until it is edited.

Set Loudness to apply equal-loudness compensation, which restores the bass and treble that the ear loses when playback is quiet. ListeningLevel is the playback level in decibels relative to the reference level, at which compensation is flat. The equaliser cannot measure the acoustic playback level, so the application sets ListeningLevel from its own volume control. The compensation is a low shelf and a high shelf that approximate the difference between the ISO 226:2023 equal-loudness contours at the reference level of 80 phon and at the listening level. The shelves run after the bands and before the output trim, and are included in AudioEffect.GetResponse(). The fit error grows with attenuation; the worst error in the ISO data range of 20 Hz to 12.5 kHz is about 0.6 dB at -10 dB, 0.9 dB at -20 dB, 2 dB at -40 dB and 3.4 dB at -60 dB, where the 1 kHz level is raised by 1.6 dB. Compensation can boost the bass by up to 30 dB at low listening levels, so place an AudioLimiter after the equaliser to prevent clipping.

Live changes crossfade the old and new filter chains over 10 ms, including output trim changes. An edit during a crossfade replaces a single queued target, which starts its own crossfade when the current one finishes. Parameter reads and AudioEffect.GetResponse() describe the latest committed target immediately, even during a transition. Device reactivation and leaving bypass reset filter history and apply the latest target without a crossfade.

The equaliser has zero algorithmic latency but its recursive state can continue producing a decay after input ends. Decay remains pending until all live filter states fall below 1e-12 internal sample units, then remaining history is discarded. Arbitrary supported poles and live edits have no fixed finite bound, so Audio.MaxDrain also limits this decay. Hard bypass and destruction can cut it abruptly.

method.name: GetBand
method.prototype: ERR eq::GetBand(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Index, struct AudioEQBand * Band)

input.param: The zero-based index of the band.
Receives the band's type, frequency, gain and Q.

description.p: Copies the committed values of the band at Index to Band. Bands can be read before initialisation, from a global equaliser, and after the equaliser has been disconnected.

result.error: Operation successful.
Index does not refer to an existing band.

method.name: InsertBand
method.comment: Inserts a band with the given values.
method.prototype: ERR eq::InsertBand(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Index, struct AudioEQBand * Band)

input.param: The position of the new band, from zero to the current band count.
The type, frequency, gain and Q of the new band.

description.p: Inserts Band at Index, moving the band at that position and every later band up by one. The new band starts with fresh filter history, while the other bands keep theirs, so a live insertion does not disturb them.

result.error: Operation successful.
Index is greater than the band count, or the equaliser already has 64 bands.
The equaliser has been disconnected from its Audio object.
Function call missing argument value(s)
A value is out of range, or Q exceeds one for a shelf after initialisation.
The equaliser is attached to the global chain.

input.param: The zero-based index of the band.

description.p: Removes the band at Index, moving every later band down by one. The remaining bands keep their filter history.

method.name: SetBand
method.comment: Replaces the values of one band.
method.prototype: ERR eq::SetBand(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Index, struct AudioEQBand * Band)

input.param: The zero-based index of the band.
The new type, frequency, gain and Q.

description.p: Replaces the type, frequency, gain and Q of the band at Index as a single change. The band keeps its filter history and a live edit crossfades to the new response. Because every value changes together, a peak can be changed to a shelf and its Q reduced to one in the same call.

field.name: Bands
field.comment: The ordered array of AudioEQBand structures.

description.p: The list can contain at most 64 bands. Replacing the list clears the filter history of every band, so use SetBand, InsertBand and RemoveBand for live adjustment; they preserve the history of the bands that they do not replace. A global equaliser accepts this field only before initialisation.

field.name: Gain
field.comment: Output trim in decibels, applied after all bands.

description.p: The range is -48 to 48 dB and the default is 0 dB. This field mirrors the gain schema key. To change it together with other parameters in a single step, use AudioEffect.Batch().

field.name: ListeningLevel
field.comment: The playback level, in decibels relative to the reference level, used for loudness compensation.

description.p: The range is -60 to 0 dB and the default is -20 dB. Set it from the application's volume control; lower levels receive more bass and treble, and compensation is flat at 0 dB. The value has no effect unless Loudness is enabled. This field mirrors the listening_level schema key. To change it together with other parameters in a single step, use AudioEffect.Batch().

Set to 1 to restore the bass and treble that the ear loses when playback is quiet, according to ListeningLevel. The default is 0 (disabled). This field mirrors the loudness schema key. To change it together with other parameters in a single step, use AudioEffect.Batch().
